Who doesn’t love a good fastback? BYD’s new Han was spotted completely undisguised, giving us an early look at its sleek design and interior ahead of its expected debut next week.

After launching the flagship Great Han last month, or the “Da Han,” as it’s called in China, BYD is preparing to introduce another newly introduced member to the lineup.

It has been revealed that BYD already sells the smaller Han, but the electric sedan is due for an overhaul. The latest version appeared in a regulatory filing by China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) last month.

According to the filing, the next-generation BYD Han will be available in three battery electric (BEV) and one plug-in hybrid (PHEV) variants.

Industry observers note that the Han EV will offer two single-motor rear-wheel-drive (RWD) options, with an output of 328 hp (245 kW) and 402 hp (300 kW). A dual-motor all-wheel-drive (AWD) version will also be offered, delivering a combined 697 hp (520 kW).

All variants use BYD’s Blade LFP Battery and are expected to be equipped with its five-minute Flash Charging technology.

The PHEV version, on the other hand, uses a 1.5-liter engine and an electric motor with up to 268 hp (200 kW).

Ahead of its expected debut at the Guangzhou Auto Show on November 27, BYD’s new Han was captured in public without any disguise.

The images sent to Autohome show a design similar to the Great Han and other upcoming Dynasty series vehicles, with its latest “Dragon Face” signature front-end look.

A few things have changed from the current model, including new headlights and a full-length light bar, while the Chinese symbol moved to the hood.

According to recent reports, from the side, the Han features a sleek, fastback silhouette. The vehicle also features a roof-mounted LiDAR to support advanced driver-assistance features. The fresh Han is expected to feature BYD’s God’s Eye B ADAS system.

According to recent reports, inside, the newly introduced Han adopts BYD’s updated interior design. The new setup includes a floating center infotainment screen and a digital instrument panel behind a three-spoke steering wheel.

The center console is also updated with two wireless phone chargers and cupholders without covers.

Doesn't matter for us here in the USA (for now), but I wish the back was a little more sedan looking with a little more trunk lid. Otherwise, nice car.

BYD’s new Han is 5,156 mm long, 1,969 mm wide, and 1,507 mm tall, with a wheelbase of 3,030 mm, which is 161 mm longer than the current version.

In a recent development, the flagship Great Han is the largest of the series, measuring 5,256 mm long. After launching the Great Han on October 13, BYD sold 4,000 units by November 1.

Since the flagship sedan starts at 235,900 yuan, or about $35,000, the smaller Han will likely be closer to 200,000 yuan ($30,000) or less. The outgoing Han starts at 168,800 yuan ($25,000).

#168404. What are those weird things on a turkey’s beak?

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (977 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Popsci ↗ Open Full Page

What are those weird things on a turkey’s beak?

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (977 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, when a tom turkey is relaxed, the fleshy growth above his beak is short and stubby, like a little unicorn horn.
  • Richard Buchholz, a professor of biology at the University of Mississippi, is the best person to ask.
  • [ Related: How did Thanksgiving turkeys get so darn major?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, when a tom turkey is relaxed, the fleshy growth above his beak is short and stubby, like a little unicorn horn. But when he struts to attract mates or establish dominance, blood rushes into the growth, known as the “snood.” The snood then swells and lengthens until it drapes over the turkey’s beak like a long pink earring. Turkey hens have snoods too, but theirs are smaller. So why would a male bird grow something that looks so impractical?

Dr. Richard Buchholz, a professor of biology at the University of Mississippi, is the best person to ask. Features of bird anatomy that seem more decorative than useful, which biologists call “ornaments,” have long fascinated Buchholz. For his master’s degree, Buchholz studied the yellow-knobbed curassow, a South American bird with a bright yellow knob on its bill and a crest of curly feathers.

[ Related: How did Thanksgiving turkeys get so darn major? ].

When it came time to choose a PhD topic, his advisor suggested a more common bird: the wild turkey. Buchholz wasn’t keen. “I don’t wanna be the turkey guy,” he told his advisor. Still, he gave it a try. More than three decades later, he’s still studying them. And his research has shown that turkey snoods have at least two functions: seduction and status.

It turns out that snoods are tools of seduction. In a 1995 study by Buchholz that used both live male turkeys and decoys, females showed a distinct preference for males with longer snoods and wider skullcaps. (The skullcap is the smooth patch of bare skin on top of a tom’s head.).

According to recent reports, this was surprising because male turkeys have several ornaments, including a beard that grows from their breast area, iridescent feathers, and a tail fan similar to that of a peacock. Yet females seem to care more about the snood and skullcap.

Lady turkeys are discerning birds. In some trials, females were choosing between two males whose snoods differed by “just a couple millimeters,” Buchholz notes—and they still went for the longer one.

He found a likely reason for this preference in male turkeys’ guts. Males with longer snoods had fewer coccidia in their digestive tract. Coccidia are single-celled parasites that damage the lining of the intestine and can be fatal in young animals.

Buchholz thinks that snoods are indicators of health, allowing females to assess a male’s quality as a mate just by looking at them. A long snood signals a male whose immune system is strong enough to fight off parasites like coccidia, and who may pass on that disease resistance to their offspring, thus improving their chances of survival.

How do birds stay warm in winter?

Do animals really mate for life?

Why are some animals so colorful? Blame this pigment.

Recent findings suggest that why do hummingbirds buzz? Tiny tornadoes.

Real-life vampire birds hunt and drink blood in remote Ecuador.

From chirps to ‘hellos’: Why some birds talk like people.

Another set of experiments, which Buchholz published in 1997, suggests that male turkeys also use snoods to size up the competition.

Buchholz trained captive male turkeys, each housed on its own, to enter an arena where bird seed was waiting. “They love bird seed,” Buchholz says. “Normally, in captivity they’re fed dry pelleted food, so they love anything that looks like a natural grain or seed.”.

Recent findings suggest that when Buchholz let two males enter the arena at the same time, they rarely engaged in a physical fight over the treat. “Almost always, one male would give up,” Buchholz says. “The male with a longer snood typically would not be the male who gave up.”.

According to recent reports, to check that the snood itself was what mattered, he ran the trials again with two plastic decoys that differed only in snood length. “And most of the males chose to eat the seed in front of the turkey decoy with the shorter snood of the two,” Buchholz claims.

A turkey’s bare head and neck are covered with featherless nodules, called caruncles, which can shift in color from red or pink to white or blue. Toms have much larger caruncles than hens. “Their color can change really dramatically at different points in a male’s display,” Buchholz states.

Sources indicate that but what it means is unknown. Buchholz suggests that the redness, rather than the size, could hint at anemia in the male, but admits that that’s just conjecture.

According to recent reports, buchholz hasn’t directly studied the function of turkey caruncles. But as part of a 2024 study he did with Rebecca Kimball of the University of Florida, he found that bare skin helps galliform birds—a group that includes turkeys, chickens, and pheasants—to lose heat and to attract mates. So caruncles may help keep a tom cool while he catches a hen’s eye.

The balancing act between body temperature regulation and courtship is the focus of Buchholz’s current research. He and his team are investigating whether rising spring temperatures affect males’ ability to display to females, and whether males choose display times and places that help them manage heat.

Buchholz has also made peace with his reputation. “I came to embrace the title of Turkey Man,” he says. “They’re really fascinating, socially interacting creatures.” As his research has shown, their anatomy is key to how they behave with each other. Those impractical-looking snoods are actually useful messaging tools—even if us humans might not find them as attractive as lady turkeys might.

#168403. Melissa Joan Hart Explains It All: Hot Flashes, Menopause, and Turning 50

📅 06 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (940 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Healthline ↗ Open Full Page

Melissa Joan Hart Explains It All: Hot Flashes, Menopause, and Turning 50

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (940 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Actor Melissa Joan Hart has a vivid memory of her mother standing in front of their open freezer to cool off.
  • It has been revealed that “[She’s] only 20 years older than me, so maybe I missed the part where she was going through [menopause], but there was no conversation about it,” Hart told Healthline.
  • Her own perimenopausal symptoms started with night sweats.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Actor Melissa Joan Hart has a vivid memory of her mother standing in front of their open freezer to cool off. As a child, she didn’t understand why. Now, as a 50-year-old woman, Hart knows that her mom was experiencing hot flashes.

It has been revealed that “[She’s] only 20 years older than me, so maybe I missed the part where she was going through [menopause], but there was no conversation about it,” Hart told Healthline. “I feel like it’s just becoming a hot topic with women, where…the taboo is going away from it now.”.

Her own perimenopausal symptoms started with night sweats.

“[It] was really jarring, and the first few times, you’re not really sure what that was…do I need to turn the air down or what’s going on here?” Hart mentioned.

Over time, she learned that she was experiencing moderate to severe hot flashes, which affect up to 80% of women during the menopause transition and can persist for 7 to 10 years.

Doctors categorize hot flashes as mild, moderate, or severe, remarked Diana Bitner, MD, OB-GYN, at Corewell Health.

According to recent reports, “[So] if they’re mild, it’s a sense of warmth (maybe in the chest, or the neck, or the face). A moderate hot flash is where there’s associated sweating, and a severe hot flash is something that stops you in your tracks, wakes you up from the middle of the night,” Bitner told Healthline.

Hart has mostly experienced hot flashes while home or at her three sons’ activities, and they have yet to interfere with her work. However, according to research, one in three women report moderate to severe challenges in managing their work due to symptoms related to menopause.

“It’s just so sad that about 10% of women leave the workforce due to menopause,” remarked Bitner. “And so it can really affect our ability to perform at these key years of not only institutional memory, but also of earning power, and it can really affect the whole community.”.

Bitner remarked women should feel empowered to bring up their menopausal symptoms or questions with their doctor.

“[This] is something that was taboo for so long…women didn’t really talk about this, whether it was because of embarrassment, or [they] weren’t sure if anyone was experiencing it,” she mentioned. “[There’s] no reason, in this day and age, we need to suffer through it…it’s something that there are treatment options for.”.

In fact, Bitner said providing specific details about their symptoms, such as how many mild, moderate, or severe hot flashes they’ve experienced over the past week, can help doctors better assess patients’ needs.

Hart aims to discuss treatment options for her hot flashes with her doctor soon. In the last few years, she noted she has put emphasis on her midlife health.

“I just was sick of waking up with aches and pains in general [thinking], ‘is this the rest of my life?’” she said.

She started listening to self-help books in the car while driving her kids around and found ways to put herself first.

“My kids are a little bit older, so I kind of have that freedom to be able to do that,” she said. “[But] along with getting older, comes the menopause, comes that different time in life. And I think it’s a good time to reevaluate [how] our bodies can’t handle what [they] used to handle, and let’s figure it out.”.

Hart has partnered with pharmaceutical company Bayer on its “Life Doesn’t Stop for a Hot Flash” campaign, which encourages women to discuss menopause symptoms with their doctors and promotes Lynkuet, a hormone-free prescription medication for moderate to severe hot flashes associated with menopause.

Sources indicate that “It’s called ‘Life Doesn’t Stop for a Hot Flash’ campaign because it shouldn’t, because we should be able to push through, and this should be a time in our lives when our kids are getting older, and we’re able to kind of reinvent ourselves,” noted Hart. “And I think it’s an exciting time, and it shouldn’t be something that we’re afraid of.”.

She is embracing speaking openly about midlife health.

“I hit 50 this year, and it was, like, a huge milestone, and I think that’s something to be proud of, and not something to shy away from,” she said.

Hart also hopes to challenge the longstanding barriers women face in Hollywood as they age, including fewer opportunities for leading roles.

“[I] think we’re seeing that the generation before, and my generation, it feels like we’re pushing those boundaries…and we’re saying, you know, that women at this age have a lot to give, have a lot of information to share, have a lot of stories to tell and experiences and adventures still ahead of us, and, you know, we’re not ready to stop,” Hart said.

In everyday life, Bitner said that while some patients avoid talking about midlife concerns like menopause with their doctors, she is seeing more patients who are confident being forthcoming.

In a recent development, as more women talk openly about menopause, she hopes to include men in the conversation, too. In fact, she invites her patients to bring their partners to appointments, so they can gain an understanding of menopause and the experiences their partners face, such as hot flashes, sleep concerns, vaginal dryness, and discomfort or pain during intercourse.

According to recent reports, “[Often], there’s, you know, comments that come up [from men who] say, ‘How do I talk about this without getting in trouble?’” noted Bitner. “[We] want everyone to join this conversation…it doesn’t have to be just her concern because we know it’s not.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that as most people in the United States know—especially around this time of the year—wild turkeys (Meleagris gallopavo) are large, broadly dark-colored birds with iridescent feathers and bald necks and heads. But not all turkeys are alike. Some of these boisterous birds have color phases, or non-traditional arrangements in their feathers, or plumage.

“Color phases are caused by genetic mutations that affect production of melanin, the pigment that causes the dark coloration in a wild turkey’s plumage,” Michael Chamberlain, National Wild Turkey Federation Endowed Chair, tells Popular Science.

According to recent reports, there are four general turkey color phases: smokey gray, erythristic, melanistic, and leucistic. Smokey gray turkeys don’t have brown pigments in their plumage, and can look white from a distance. Leucistic turkeys have white feathers because they lack melanin production in their plumage, but their heads, beards, and legs appear more normal and red.

According to recent reports, melanistic birds are essentially the opposite. The genetic mutation causes an overproduction of melanin, so the turkey is darker-colored and almost totally black. Erythristic turkeys have an overproduction of carotenoids (types of pigments behind orange, yellow, and red colors) that prevent the production of melanin and also make their feathers more reddish.

Recent findings suggest that how common these different color variations are is still a question, because experts have just started to track their occurrences. Leucistic birds appear to be present throughout North America, while melanistic birds—the completely black ones—seem to be more rare.

In a recent development, “It’s unknown how odd plumage affects survival or reproduction, but it’s logical to assume that lighter colored birds and particularly leucistic and smoke phase birds would be obvious to predators,” explains Chamberlain, who is also known as the Wild Turkey Doc. However, “the relationship between odd plumage and survival or reproduction has never been documented in the literature.”.

But if you come across a picture of a gorgeously-colored bird that looks like a turkey-shaped peacock, chances are that you’re looking at the only other turkey species: the ocellated turkey (Meleagris ocellata). These fantastical looking animals are the wild turkey’s tropical cousin and only exist in the Yucatán Peninsula, and  were domesticated by the ancient Maya.

Feel free to talk turkey with these and other fun turkey facts this Thanksgiving.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that A well-known ancient Egyptian curse is not only older than historians thought—the curse that called upon the sun god’s wrath upon one’s enemies was much more commonly employed than experts assumed.
  • Prior to finding the 40 charred remnants, the only documentation of the Apophis ritual was a ritual manual dating back to the late fourth century BCE.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that A well-known ancient Egyptian curse is not only older than historians thought—the curse that called upon the sun god’s wrath upon one’s enemies was much more commonly employed than experts assumed. However, the upcoming evidence concerning the “Apophis ritual” wasn’t recently discovered in an excavated spellbook. According to a study published in the Journal of the Egyptian Language and Antiquities, archaeologists learned the latest details from postage stamp-sized papyrus fragments left in 3,400-year-old trash piles.

Prior to finding the 40 charred remnants, the only documentation of the Apophis ritual was a ritual manual dating back to the late fourth century BCE. Egyptian priests originally designed the spell to aid the sun god Ra against Apophis, his eternal foe and the snake god of chaos, fire, and darkness. Others later adapted the ritual to curse enemies of the pharaoh and counter problems associated with the serpent like inclement weather and poisons. But although researchers initially assumed the Apophis ritual was reserved for religious leaders, the papyrus fragments retrieved from temple ruins at Thebes have dramatically expanded its audience.

“They show that the ritual was much older than the one surviving copy from the fourth century [BCE] might suggest,” Fredrik Hagen, an Egyptologist at the University of Copenhagen and study co-author, remarked in a statement. “Already 1,000 years earlier, during what we call the New Kingdom, it was an integrated part of Egyptian culture.”.

While additional analysis of the fragments revealed that such rituals were widespread in ancient Egypt, Hagen explained that additional contextual references to the Apophis incantation indicate it was a “common feature” in daily life.

“We know that literate people, including those who were not priests, had access to magical rituals and functioned as magicians and healers,” he stated. “It is clear that people approached scribes for help in performing magic, both for protection and for attacking others.”.

The existence of the remnants are surprising in their own right, given what the ritual required. Their charring is only part of the necessary curse protocols—prior to burning the written spells, practitioners stepped on the papyrus, stabbed it with a knife, and even spit on it.

“For the ritual to be successful, the materials had to be destroyed by fire, so we are extremely fortunate to have found any of them in a condition that still allows them to be recognized and studied,” stated Hagen.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Social media influencers claim that having a “ferritin face” may indicate you’re low in iron.

Ferritin is a protein that helps your body store iron. You need iron in order to make healthy red blood cells, which carry oxygen from your lungs to the rest of your body. Iron is also notable for bone marrow, organs, healthy muscles, and brain development.

As “ferritin face” makes its way across social media platforms, users are describing several tell-tale signs, including:.

Owners have also shared images of their face before and after taking iron supplements or getting an iron infusion. Videos about “ferritin face” have garnered millions of views on various platforms.

However, medical professionals state that your appearance alone is not enough to diagnose iron deficiency.

According to recent reports, “It’s vital to understand that ferritin face is not a medical diagnosis, nor is it a confirmed symptom of iron deficiency. While some people with iron deficiency can appear pale due to low hemoglobin levels in their red blood cells, there are many other symptoms to consider,” noted Daniel Atkinson, a general practitioner in the United Kingdom and clinical lead at Treated.

“Notably, these symptoms are also present in many different conditions, and their presence does not necessarily mean iron deficiency anemia or even low ferritin levels. Similar features are seen in people with iron processing and absorption problems, such as gluten intolerance, or in urgent sudden blood loss scenarios,” added Jonathan Jennings, MD, board certified internist at Medical Offices of Manhattan.

Recent findings suggest that iron deficiency can affect your skin and appearance. These signs are often subtle, but may include:.

Industry observers note that in some ways, the social media videos are correct. Your skin and face can change when your iron levels are low.

“The facial signs people point to, like pale skin and a washed-out look, mostly come from anaemia, when your haemoglobin has dropped. But iron deficiency and anaemia aren’t the same thing,” stated Thom Phillips, a general practitioner in the United Kingdom and Chief Medical Officer at Forth. “By the time low iron shows on your face, your stores are usually close to empty.”.

It is key to speak with a healthcare professional, who will run blood tests such as a complete blood count and ferritin levels.

It is also key not to take iron supplements without first checking with your healthcare professional, because having too much iron in your body can also cause negative effects.

Too little and too much iron could raise your risk of infection, which is why it’s notable not to take supplements without medical supervision.

The signs and symptoms of iron deficiency can depend on whether you are anemic or not. Some of the early signs may include:.

“These symptoms typically occur because your body produces fewer red blood cells, which results in less oxygen being delivered throughout your body, making you feel tired and weak,” stated Atkinson.

Less common symptoms may include:.

While your facial appearance can be a sign that something isn’t right, healthcare professionals consider other symptoms and how you feel overall.

They also rely on blood tests to confirm the diagnosis and guide treatment.

“The misinformation is the idea that you can spot it yourself. That leads to two problems: people with low iron who look fine assume they’re OK, and people who look tired start taking iron supplements they don’t need,” said Phillips.

Atkinson also noted that factors such as different settings and environmental conditions can affect how your face appears.

That being mentioned, the “ferritin face” trend may help bring awareness to certain symptoms and when to get them checked.

“[This] trend may raise some awareness about iron deficiency anemia and how low iron levels can impact daily life,” mentioned Atkinson.

Recent findings suggest that “Fatigue and lightheadedness are common side effects of low iron, but it manifests in other ways too, such as paler skin or increased hair shedding, which can be concerning for many people. If you experience these symptoms, you should let your doctor know so they can help treat the condition appropriately,” he noted.

#168392. Tech Report: What Elizabeth Holmes's Stare Doesn’t Say

📅 27 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (825 w)

Tech Report: What Elizabeth Holmes's Stare Doesn’t Say

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (825 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s documentary You Can See Everything, the camera cuts to a tight close-up of the upper half of Elizabeth Holmes’s face.
  • According to recent reports, holmes’s partner, Billy Evans, has the same wide blue eyes and unblinking gaze.
  • Blinking is a coordinated sensorimotor action that protects the eyes while reflecting shifts in attention and cognitive load.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 27, 2026 | Reviewed by Lybi Ma.

In Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s documentary You Can See Everything, the camera cuts to a tight close-up of the upper half of Elizabeth Holmes’s face. Her large blue eyes hold Fielder’s gaze for an extraordinarily long time without blinking. It was quite distracting. I found myself counting the seconds between blinks and trying to match them. I couldn’t keep up.

According to recent reports, holmes’s partner, Billy Evans, has the same wide blue eyes and unblinking gaze. It was unnerving to watch them even in the safety of my own living room.

Blinking is a coordinated sensorimotor action that protects the eyes while reflecting shifts in attention and cognitive load. Adults typically blink about 14 to 17 times per minute, with each blink lasting roughly 100 to 300 milliseconds.

People naturally blink less when they’re working hard to focus. Studies in cognitive and auditory neuroscience show that people systematically blink less during moments of high cognitive demand. For example, people blink less in noisy environments so they don’t miss visual cues like lip movement.

Holmes and Evans don’t just blink less; their wide-eyed look demonstrates white around the iris. This effect comes from how far the eyelids open, not how often they close. Put the two together—wide-open lids and a low blink rate—and you get a jarring laser-focused stare. The iris, an orb floating in a white sea of sclera.

In a recent development, research by Tamami Nakano found that people watching someone speak tend to sync their blinks with the speaker's. When I tried to match Holmes's blinks and failed, I was consciously doing what viewers do without noticing.

Psychologists Sharon Leal and Aldert Vrij found that people blinked less when they lied and blinked more than usual right afterward. Their 2008 research concluded that lying is cognitively demanding. Blinking slows while the lie is being told, then rebounds once it's over.

Recent findings suggest that I’m not suggesting Holmes is a liar. Someone who blinks less might be lying, but they may also be concentrating, self-conscious in front of a camera, on medication, or simply a person who blinks less than average. A low blink rate, in and of itself, suggests someone may be working hard. It doesn’t tell us at what.

Holmes’s stare also reminded me of Anthony Hopkins’s Oscar-winning performance as Hannibal Lecter in The Silence of the Lambs. Hopkins said in an interview that he deliberately minimized blinking while playing the cannibalistic serial killer. The result was an unflinching performance that made Lecter feel oddly calm, predatory, and menacing.

Sources indicate that while popular culture associates unblinking stares with sociopathy, the research doesn’t support it. In fact, some studies suggest that people high in psychopathic traits pay less attention to other people’s eyes, not more. An unblinking stare is not a reliable indicator of a personality disorder. It can be an effective tool for an actor or for a young founder delivering a TEDMED talk, as Holmes did in 2014. But it’s not diagnostic.

It has been revealed that in the 2005 bestseller Blink: The Power of Thinking Without Thinking, author Malcolm Gladwell argued that snap judgments and first impressions formed within the first two seconds can be just as accurate as slow, deliberate analysis. “There can be as much value in the blink of an eye as in months of rational analysis,” he wrote.

Gladwell wasn’t writing about literal blinking, but he attached a condition that matters here: fast judgments are trustworthy only when they’re grounded in real experience.

Sources indicate that my first reaction to Holmes and Evans was a snap judgment. I don’t have any real expertise in reading blink rates. What I have is a cultural script (Hannibal Lecter, the wide-eyed villain) and an expectation about conversational rhythm, which includes blinking and looking away occasionally.

That doesn’t make my unease any less valid. It was real information about me. It told me that Holmes’s stare had broken a social rhythm, and that I was primed to read that break as menace.

The documentary title promises we can see everything. The close-up on Holmes’s eyes reminds us we can’t. All we can see is that she isn’t blinking. We can’t see why.

Gillespie, S. M., Rotshtein, P., Wells, L. J., Beech, A. R., & Mitchell, I. J. (2015). Psychopathic traits are associated with reduced attention to the eyes of emotional faces among adult male non-offenders. Frontiers in Human Neuroscience, 9, 552.

It has been revealed that gladwell, M. (2005). Blink: The Power of Thinking Without Thinking. Little, Brown.

While the files uploaded to the agency’s Freedom of Information Act online reading room may not offer definitive proof of the cryptid’s existence, they may help redirect unwanted political conversations at the Thanksgiving table this year.

It has been revealed that “I don’t know if I believe in the Bigfoot theory, but the tracks were right there,” an 87-year-old resident of Sanders County, Montana, told his local newspaper in 2003 after discovering some suspicious footprints. “What else could it be?”.

Recent findings suggest that another file also focuses on purported cryptid tracks in the summer of 1982. In that case, park rangers were actually dispatched to obtain plaster molds of footprints reported in Oregon’s Umatilla National Forest.Unfortunately, resource staffer Roger Baker didn’t sound impressed by what he found on June 17, 1982.

“It is my opinion that the tracks…were made by something other than a 300-pound-plus, two footed being,” Baker explained, although he did concede that the prints appeared “very natural.”.

The final archival document is a local resident’s somewhat rambling personal account of the history of Petty Creek, a forested area located about 30 miles west of Missoula, Montana. Among stories of ill-fated gold prospectors, camel importation, and buried treasure, Leo Kinney tells of his own near-brush with Bigfoot. According to Kinney, he and some fellow hunters didn’t actually see the hairy biped walking around, but they saw evidence of its recent presence.

“Tracks, a strong odor, and grunting were observed,” he wrote in 1980.

According to recent reports, the U.S. Forestry Service’s archival uploads are fun reads, but many Sasquatch believers are still reeling from the recent release of Capturing Bigfoot. Released in October, the critically acclaimed documentary delves into the story behind the Patterson–Gimlin tape. The controversial home video recording is widely considered the most famous Bigfoot sighting of all time, although the film essentially confirms once-and-for-all that the grainy footage was a carefully constructed hoax.

GM Energy and WeaveGrid are launching a vehicle-to-grid (V2G) pilot that will let select Southern California Edison (SCE) customers send electricity from their EV batteries back to the grid. Eligible drivers could get more than $16,000 in help with equipment and installation, and earn money when the grid needs their power.

GM says the pilot participants will be its first EV drivers in California to export power from their cars to their homes. Through the California Energy Commission, eligible customers in SCE’s Emergency Load Reduction Program can get up to $8,000 toward a GM Energy V2H system and up to $8,099 toward eligible installation costs, including connecting the system to the grid.

Chevy, GMC, and Cadillac EV drivers can use time-of-use energy management to take advantage of lower rates and may be paid for participating in eligible demand-response events. How much they save or earn depends on their rate plan, electricity use, and participation.

GM already offers managed charging through 13 utilities, and each program varies by utility.

An EV battery stores direct current (DC), and your house and the grid use alternating current (AC). GM’s current home backup system uses a wall-mounted inverter to convert the power. With AC bidirectional charging, the car’s onboard inverter does the job. Moving that work into the car could make the equipment on your garage wall simpler and cheaper to install.

In a recent development, not in CA, but we use solar, time of use, and EVs to minimize our energy costs. We’re not feeding power back to the grid from our cars, but the combo of TOU, solar and EVs does allow us to reduce costs significantly. Solar covers all the expensive peak power, I have the cars start charging early enough to use any extra solar, and the rest is off peak at half cost.

Sources indicate that GM is joining CharIN‘s North American AC V2G task force, which is working to align technical standards, equipment certification, and utility approval requirements. In Southern California, the pilot will give GM and its partners a look at how the process works for drivers, from signing up and getting the hardware installed to getting utility approval and sending power back.

  • As antithetical as an EV might be to the point of a Boxster, this 718 looks, dances, and even sounds (on the inside) like the flat-six-powered machine we’ve known and loved for years.
  • Where Porsche put the 800-volt battery pack in the Boxster flips the “every EV drives the same” trope on its side.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the most key detail about the electric Porsche 718 Boxster isn’t that it’s an EV, it’s that it’s a Porsche sports car. The fresh electric sports car will be officially unveiled next month, but before then, Porsche is offering up a few details on a black-and-red-camoed platter. More important, beyond the limited intel, I got to spin laps in a prototype at the Porsche Experience Center Los Angeles. I also rode shotgun while an engineer hotfooted it through the Angeles National Forest.

I won’t keep you in suspense. As antithetical as an EV might be to the point of a Boxster, this 718 looks, dances, and even sounds (on the inside) like the flat-six-powered machine we’ve known and loved for years. What Porsche put together is an electric car that tries harder than any before at copying the experience of a mid-engine sports car. And there’s a lot more to it than just fake noises.

Where Porsche put the 800-volt battery pack in the Boxster flips the “every EV drives the same” trope on its side. Instead of the industry-standard floor-positioned battery pack, the 718 stuffs it exactly where the internal-combustion engine was traditionally housed in the Boxster: right behind the driver’s head. This changes the weight balance from the EV-typical 50/50 to a much more mid-engine-sports-car-like 40/60. The car’s polar moment of inertia is undeniably behind you, a fresh sensation in the world of electric cars. Maserati planned something similar for the MC20 Folgore but canceled that project before it made production.

Sources indicate that other massive benefits come with this battery arrangement. Engineers have been able to position the seats just as low in the floor as in the gas-powered Boxster, maintaining a proper sports-car driving position. I can promise nobody will be begging for it to be lower. It helps the design too. While this prototype was covered in camouflage, it was evident that there wasn’t a thick battery pack ruining the Boxster’s proportions. Also unaffected by the transition to electric power are the Boxster trunk and frunk. Just by eyeballing them I could tell that they look to be nearly identical to the previous car in terms of capaciousness.

Sources indicate that deciding how large the battery pack should be was one of the biggest problems Porsche had to solve. We’ll need to wait for the reveal to know the car’s range and battery capacity, but everything is a trade-off when it comes to an electric sports car. All we know about its curb weight is that an “intelligent lightweight construction” will yield a vehicle weight “similar to current 911 models.”.

It has been revealed that for reference, a 911 GTS Cabriolet presently comes in around 3700 pounds. After many, many laps around the Porsche Experience Center, my gut tells me the Boxster weighs somewhere in the 3700–4000-pound range. Or, in other words, exceptional for an EV. And not so great compared with the outgoing 718 GTS 4.0, which managed to weigh in under 3200 pounds.

Sources indicate that without range figures to go by, my only reference point for expectations was that the car flashed a “be mindful of range” warning after about 40 minutes of push laps on Porsche’s track. There are plenty of gas-powered sports cars that would be needing a fresh tank at that point too, although obviously not 911s equipped with the extended-range fuel tank.

Sources indicate that audible entertainment is handled by Porsche’s E-Shift system, which will come standard. This virtual simulation of a PDK transmission and engine noise debuted in the Taycan, and the new Boxster is equipped with its own version of the software. Press the button on the steering wheel, and the naturally aspirated flat-six from the 981-generation Boxster GTS springs to life over speakers both inside and outside the car.

Industry observers note that engineers painstakingly measured, recorded, and reproduced the sound, then emulated a seven-speed PDK for you to shift through. Unlike the Hyundai Ioniq 5 N or the Genesis GV60 Magma, Porsche does not simulate a gas engine’s torque curve in E-Shift, preferring to maximize performance over experience. That noted, there are still some theatrics to be found. Downshifting supports “engine” braking via electric-motor regen, and you even hear the “exhaust” popping and crackling on the overrun.

According to recent reports, for many Porsche enthusiasts, it won’t be enough, especially when you remove the roof. The speakers are smart in that Porsche is able to simulate the noise as though it’s coming from behind you in traditional mid-engine fashion. But the spell is easily broken when the wind overpowers the speakers, or you gun it past a wall and there’s no delicious mechanical flat-six howl echoing back at you. It’s fake. I could tell straightaway. And everyone else will too.

It has been revealed that but alas! I had exponentially more fun driving the Boxster with E-Shift than without, especially on the track. You can choose between manual and automatic gearchanges, and I largely left it in automatic. Hearing and remembering where the “engine” revved as I approached the braking zone helped me learn the track swiftly and pick out my braking points by sound alone, very similar to Road & Track’s first experience in the BMW M3 EV prototype running a comparable system.

Recent findings suggest that then on corner exit, it supplied a faithful throttle reference that helped me trace little slides out of tighter turns in the permissive PSM Sport traction mode. As soon as I turned E-Shift off, I felt lost on the track. And call me old-fashioned, but silently skittering between corners with just the sound of tire squeal is sad. Even more so, because this chassis is a damn good one.

According to recent reports, porsche is being coy with the finer details but let on that numerous chassis components are based on those found in the 911. Boxster owners will be familiar with this hand-me-down strategy, and it continues into the electric era. The steering, braking system, and wheel-and-tire combinations are based on the 911. Pirelli P Zero R summer tires were fitted to staggered wheels (20s in front and 21s in rear) for my time in the car, with a 255-section width in front and a 305-section width in the rear. The newly introduced car has PASM damping tech, and engineers note both the damper and spring calibration are softer than those in an equivalent 911. The suspension’s controlled but comfortable composure over rough sections of the road confirmed as much. Thankfully, the brakes just felt like brakes with no weird regen sensation and plenty of feel at the limit.

It has been revealed that my test car didn’t have it, but a sport suspension will also be available. And for the first time, the 718 gets optional rear-axle steering, not to help tighten its turning radius but to supply greater stability at high speeds where the rear wheels can turn in coordination with the fronts. There’s even a front-axle lift, picking up where the Spyder RS left off as the first Boxster with mentioned feature.

Sources indicate that the powertrain itself is all good news. Porsche wouldn’t supply an output number, but the car I drove employs a single electric motor in the rear. It’s reportedly powerful enough for a 0–60-mph run in under three seconds. Porsche says it will be the most powerful 718 so far, meaning more than the 493-hp output of the GT4 RS, and it will almost certainly be the quickest to 60 too. As with Porsche’s other EVs, there’s a push-to-pass mode you can activate for 10 seconds at a time, and using launch control unleashes maximum output too. But at no point was I wanting for more punch around the relatively tight track. Once the tires warmed, launching was effortless, and I didn’t doubt the sub-three-second claim for a moment. The same goes for the road drive, where the Boxster is powerful enough to need serious restraint to not end up doing jail speeds.

In a recent development, porsche Torque Vectoring Plus, another feature derived from the 911, helps dole out power between the two rear wheels to maximum effectiveness. Between this power-distribution system and the Boxster’s happy tendency to kindly bend itself into corners under braking, this 718 has the balance and more jovial nature of the previous one. But another trait carries over: The rear indicates a tendency to dance further out than you would expect from an EV with a more typical 50/50 weight distribution. And despite that Porsche puts massive emphasis on keeping weight down (it even reduced the charge ports from its typical two to only one), there was no denying that this Boxster felt porkier than before. The difference was most obvious in the tighter corners where the mass couldn’t be disguised and the grippy front tires ultimately surrendered to the sheer weight that is being asked to turn.

Porsche says it will be launching the electric Boxster into the world with two versions to start. While it wouldn’t reveal the trims, I do know that the version I drove will be the spicier of the two, therefore corresponding with the previous Boxster S. I can’t be certain whether it’s a hit or a miss until I experience the final production car, but I can say this is much more than simply an electric powertrain transplant.

It challenges the hard-core among us in ways EVs simply haven’t before, and if it’s not your cup of tea, don’t worry. Porsche will keep making gas-powered performance cars. It’s just a shame that they won’t start under $100,000, where this one is projected to begin.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • An international team of scientists conducting a deep-sea survey of the Great Australian Bight discovered the clam.
  • In a recent development, they found V.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the fact that a latest clam species (Vaticinaria gulicola) was discovered where the sun does not shine may be the least interesting thing about this bivalve. V. gulicola lives inside of a deep-sea urchin. The clam appears to have made a little home for itself inside the urchin’s oesophagus, the tube that runs through the center of the urchin’s body and into the intestine. A study recently published in the journal ZooKeys details this highly unusual partnership.

An international team of scientists conducting a deep-sea survey of the Great Australian Bight discovered the clam. The survey studied the seafloor at depths of 656 to 16,404 feet deep and uncovered 66,721 invertebrates representing 1,267 species. About a third of these species are believed to be newly introduced to science—including this quirky clam.

In a recent development, they found V. gulicola along the abyssal seafloor at depths of about 13,000 to 16,400 feet. At this depth, sunlight cannot penetrate the water column. During these deep trawls, the team found clams equipped with threads for attaching to a host, but did not see any hosts. Additional searching revealed more clams lodged inside thin, slippery tubes. They analyzed the DNA of these tubes and discovered that they were the oesophagus of the urchin Carnarechinus clypeatus.

It has been revealed that “We were absolutely stunned to find this bivalve living inside the throat of a deepwater sea urchin,” Paul Valentich-Scott, a study co-author and marine malacologist at the Santa Barbara Museum of Natural History, mentioned in a statement. “A Russian scientist [Alexander Mironov] originally thought these clams were being eaten by the sea urchin, but we later determined that it was actually living inside the oesophagus.”.

Sources indicate that mironov had noticed clams inside the urchin’s gut as far back as the 1970s and 1990s. The team also found related clams living inside of a specimen of the same urchin that was collected during the Challenger Expedition (1872 to 1876), where they had gone unnoticed for over a century.

In a recent development, most clam species that live with other animals cling to the outside of their host. Endocommensalism, or living inside of the host, is more rare. The fresh clam’s genus Vaticinaria is only the second clam genus of its superfamily known to live this way.

“Endocommensalism is extremely rare in galeommatids and all bivalves,” Valentich-Scott added. “Most commensal bivalves attach to the outside of their host. This latest species lives inside its throat.”.

Recent findings suggest that this fresh clam shows no obvious adaptations to life inside a host. It is about 0.74 inches long, which is large for its group, and has a shell that closes fully. The species name gulicola comes from the Latin word for “throat” and “inhabitant.” Much about the clam remains unknown and will require further study.

“We know very little about this upcoming species or its sea urchin host,” mentioned Valentich-Scott. “The host sea urchin has never been collected intact, so we really don’t even know what it looks like. We have no idea how this bivalve can live inside the throat of the urchin, or what it eats.”.

It has been revealed that the team suspects that the clams can feed off the nutrient-rich sediment that the urchin eats, but this hasn’t been studied. Further deep-sea sampling should reveal more about this clam and other unusual creatures of the deep-sea.

NHL may not be a household name, but its all-latest, all-electric NTE240E ultra-class haul track could change that with a 240 ton payload, over 4.1 MWh of battery, advanced regenerative braking, and a world’s first double-gun MCS charging setup.

In a recent development, for the uninitiated, Inner Mongolia North Hauler Joint Stock Co., Ltd. (NHL) is a Chinese heavy equipment manufacturer specializing in the enormous rigid-frame haul trucks used in open-pit mining operations. Established in 1988, NHL has decades of experience building mining trucks for customers around the world, including some of the industry’s largest diesel-electric hybrids. The brand’s new NTE240E is different, representing a organization’s real push into battery-electric mining equipment, and it’s powering that push with some seriously ambitious technology.

According to recent reports, let’s start with the battery. The NTE240E packs an absolutely MASSIVE battery pack, with the highest-capacity versions offering up to 4,100 kWh (4.1 MWh) of onboard energy storage. Keeping that much battery topped off is no small task, which is why NHL developed an equally ambitious energy replenishment strategy supporting dual-gun MCS charging, allowing its town-sized battery to go from 20% to 90% in under an hour.

That means operators can take advantage of shift changes and scheduled rest breaks to top off the battery without sacrificing an entire work shift to charging – but even more impressive than the fact that all that juice can be crammed into so big a battery in so little time is the fact that, according to NHL, it can be done at just 25°C (about 77°F).

It has been revealed that plugging in isn’t the only way the NTE240E drinks its juice. NHL’s latest dynamic power reception system uses overhead current collectors to supply electricity directly to the truck while it’s climbing loaded mine roads, allowing it to then “ride the brakes” for more energy all the way downhill.

The combined technologies allow NHL’s operators to keep the massive trucks moving without relying entirely on their onboard batteries. The result is a claimed 15% improvement in energy efficiency over the ultra-class industry average.

Sources indicate that that efficiency turns into savings, which means the economics of running an NTE240E could be just as compelling as the emissions savings – and those are substantial. NHL says each NTE240E can reduce harmful carbon emissions by more than 2,000 tons annually, even as it cuts operating costs by more than 60% compared to a comparably capable diesel.

According to recent reports, what’s more, because the substantial BEV’s electrical system eliminates the need for engine-related hardware like generators and the maintenance and overhaul costs associated with those components. Taken as a whole, the NHL seems to be a compelling offering … but that’s not for me to say. You guys are the experts – let us know what you think of the new NHL NTE240E, in the comments.

#168385. Mammograms May Offer Early Insight Into Cardiovascular Disease

📅 08 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (823 w)

Mammograms May Offer Early Insight Into Cardiovascular Disease

📅 08 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (823 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mammograms are widely used to help detect breast cancer, but they may also offer insight into heart health.
  • The routine X-ray screening may identify breast arterial calcification (BAC), which is the presence of calcium deposits within the walls of the small arteries in the breast.
  • On a mammogram, BAC is commonly identified as thin, white, parallel lines that give a “tram-track” appearance.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mammograms are widely used to help detect breast cancer, but they may also offer insight into heart health.

The routine X-ray screening may identify breast arterial calcification (BAC), which is the presence of calcium deposits within the walls of the small arteries in the breast.

On a mammogram, BAC is commonly identified as thin, white, parallel lines that give a “tram-track” appearance.

According to recent reports, while BAC is harmless to the breasts, it is associated with a significantly higher risk of cardiovascular disease. A 2022 study found women with BAC were 51% more likely to develop heart disease or experience a stroke than those without it.

Laxmi Mehta, MD, a cardiologist at The Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center, said BAC is associated with cardiovascular risk factors, such as diabetes, high blood pressure, and high cholesterol. Additionally, BAC has been connected to:.

“The reasons for BAC resulting in higher risks for cardiovascular disease are not definitely determined; however, there are some potential mechanisms, one being that they share similar risk factors that result in vascular injury or metabolic stress that result in vascular calcification and atherosclerosis,” Mehta told Healthline.

Cheng-Han Chen, MD, interventional cardiologist and medical director of the Structural Heart Program at MemorialCare Saddleback Medical Center, added that because BAC and heart disease share many of the same risk factors, “calcium in breast arteries therefore suggests disease in the heart (coronary) and brain arteries as well,” he told Healthline.

While 1 in 39 females in the United States dies from breast cancer each year, cardiovascular disease causes one out of every three deaths, resulting in 1 death per minute.

“Cardiovascular disease is still the most common cause of death in premenopausal women,” Richard Reitherman, MD, PhD, a radiologist and medical director of breast imaging at MemorialCare Breast Center at Orange Coast Medical Center, told Healthline.

“The presentation of cardiovascular disease in premenopausal women is notoriously different than in postmenopausal women, primarily [because] there are no typical symptoms such as chest pain.”.

Reitherman mentioned that a prevalent and common health screening procedure such as a mammogram can lead to the early identification of women with silent cardiovascular disease.

“Cardiovascular outcome studies that have included breast arterial calcifications as a risk factor are increasingly reported in the medical literature,” he remarked.

“The hope is that identifying younger women with silent cardiovascular risks [like BAC along with] appropriate integrated risk identification, analysis, and interventions can significantly reduce mortality in this age group.”.

Mehta remarked there are several reasons BAC has been overlooked as a risk factor for heart disease.

“Mammograms are completed for assessment of breast cancer, and BAC has been historically an ‘incidental’ finding, which is not clinically relevant from an oncologic standpoint,” she said.

Additionally, there is no standardization on quantification of BAC severity, nor is it a required component of mammogram reports, noted Mehta.

However, routine reporting of BAC on mammograms is an urgent goal of the American College of Radiology, Society of Breast Imaging, and Medicare, said Reitherman.

It has been revealed that in fact, it is gaining traction in the United States. A latest Maryland law, passed on October 1, requires mammography centers to notify women when a BAC is detected on their mammogram.

“Automated identification and reporting of these calcifications detected on screening mammograms will become increasingly prevalent in the coming months [and] years,” said Reitherman.

The next step is to identify this group of women to primary care physicians so that appropriate risk evaluation can take place, Reitherman added.

In addition to doctors routinely screening for conditions related to heart disease, such as diabetes, high blood pressure, and high cholesterol, he hopes BAC will also be routinely considered.

“Under current development are protocols to identify patients needing a cardiologist’s training and expertise to appropriately stratify this group of patients,” remarked Reitherman.

“The common healthcare behavior [of] having regular mammograms not only reduces risk of morbidity and mortality from breast cancer but will hopefully contribute to the reduction of morbidity and mortality from cardiovascular disease in younger women.”.

He mentioned this type of integrated healthcare approach demonstrates cross-specialty integration and coordination among women, radiologists, and their healthcare providers to improve women’s lives.

“This is an amazing game-changing opportunity,” Reitherman said.

Mehta said it’s reasonable for women to ask if BAC is present on their mammogram report.

“But if it is not uniformly reported by the radiologist, the individual clinician may not have the answer,” she said.

More research is needed before BAC on mammograms can be used routinely to predict heart disease.

Finding out your BAC could provide additional information to help you and your doctors decide how aggressively to address your cardiovascular risk factors, Chen stated.

It has been revealed that reitherman agreed. “The goal of reducing morbidity and mortality from any cause such as cardiovascular disease is based on recognition of risk factors, followed by appropriate lifestyle and pharmacologic interventions,” he mentioned.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • I liked running and endurance-based activities because I felt like they complimented sports pretty well, especially lacrosse, which eventually became my main activity.
  • Industry observers note that in the middle of college, everyone was sent home because of the pandemic.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As soon as I started walking, I was playing a sport. I don’t remember there being a time where I wasn't on a sports team during my childhood. To me, exercise was practice after school and traveling for games on the weekend for whatever sport I was playing. As a teen, in my off-seasons, my mom would beg me to go to the gym with her for fun, but I didn't have much interest in it.

I liked running and endurance-based activities because I felt like they complimented sports pretty well, especially lacrosse, which eventually became my main activity. I ended up being able to play lacrosse in college, where I was first required to start strength training to prepare for the season. While I was in shape for my sport, I couldn’t even lift the bar in the gym, and I was mesmerized by all the different movements that I didn’t really understand.

Industry observers note that in the middle of college, everyone was sent home because of the pandemic. I felt far away from my entire life and all my friends, and like there was nothing for me to be doing. There was so much time on my hands, and there was nowhere for me to be.

While sitting at home alone, I had nothing to do besides work out. To pass the time and cope with what was happening, I wanted to exercise, but I felt stuck since gyms were closed.

It has been revealed that then my dad handed me this 25-pound bag of rice from Costco and noted, “You can train with this. There’s actually a lot you can do with it.” So I stuffed that bag of rice in a backpack to make it heavy, and I’d use it as a weight. I would put the backpack at the front of my body and do squats. I would use it as a kettlebell for kettlebell swings. I would put it on my back and do walking lunges.

I realized there was a lot I could do at home, but I wanted to try to strength train at the actual gym. I decided that, when I was done playing college lacrosse, I would get serious about a gym routine.

When I graduated from college, I was excited—but so confused—about where to begin. I followed fitness influencers on TikTok who gave workout tips and advice on which movements to try. But I also wanted to make sure all of my information was accurate and science-based, so I started researching online, watching the moves other people at the gym were doing, and reaching out to my old college coaches for tips.

Recent findings suggest that at first, I thought I needed to be running and lifting every day to stay fit, but I soon realized I was over-exerting my body. I started learning more about the basics of strength training and how to work different muscles with compound movements like squats, deadlifts, hang cleans, and more. I also learned how to supplement those movements by doing auxiliary exercises with dumbbells or body weight exercises like curls, lunges, and more.

It has been revealed that after a combination of trial and error, researching, and practicing at the gym, I finally found my strength training routine and stride. I started to finally perfect my strength exercises. My confidence was growing so much as a result, which only motivated me to continue. I developed so much discipline that translated into every other aspect of my life.

Sources indicate that even when things got off-routine for me, I could fall back into strength training to find my rhythm again. I know it’ll always be there, giving me structure even when everything else feels unsettled.

When I first started lifting, I was hungrier because I was training more, but I was afraid to eat more. But if you want to build muscle, you need protein and you have to eat! It’s how your body survives and thrives. You need to take care of yourself, and that includes getting enough sleep.

According to recent reports, I do not always feel motivated to workout. That’s just how life is. But when I started strength training, I developed so much discipline. Even when I don’t have motivation, that discipline is there now, not just at the gym. Stick with it and allow that habit to form.

It’s honestly true when they say that movement is medicine. When I'm taking care of my body, even if my mental headspace isn't in peak condition, I feel better after movement. It’s not all about hitting personal bests, either. (Though those certainly help!) I might tell myself, “I don't want to go to the gym today, but I will because I know it’s good for me.” Strength training gives me the confidence to know I can do anything I set my mind to.

Industry observers note that nowadays, I strength train four days a week, and I’ll also do a designated cardio day. I base my training on muscle groups.

Each workout will have a main exercise, such as a squat, bench press, or deadlift. Then, I pair them with auxiliary exercises like lunges, quad extensions, hamstring curls, rear delt flies, incline dumbbell bench presses, and more that target smaller muscles.

Recent findings suggest that I try to stay between four to five exercises per workout so I don't overdo it. I like to keep it simple when I write my workout looks. I’ll follow those plans for a certain number of weeks depending on my goals, then I’ll move on from there. I like to keep things interesting for myself to ensure I never get bored, because I want to be able to do this forever.

It has been revealed that I used to not be able to hang clean the bar, and once I even dropped it on my knee and ruptured my bursa. It was all bruised, and I was so embarrassed. From then on, I had a real mental block with hang cleans. I told myself, “I’m never going to be able to do a lot of weight.”.

According to recent reports, years later, I decided it was about time I face my fear. I worked my way up to being able to put 25-pound plates on each side, coming out to about 100 pounds, depending on the bar. The more I practiced, the easier it became for me, and getting there was a huge milestone.

Recent findings suggest that any upper-body movements are especially empowering to me. Many people don’t think you can have impressive upper-body strength as a woman. When I was able to work my way up to putting a 45-pound weight on each side for bench presses, coming out to 135 pounds, I felt unstoppable. It was such a massive deal to me since I never thought I’d be able to do it. It’s such an empowering feeling to be doing something that a lot of people see as something only men would do.

Turkeys may be getting all of the bird hype this week, but plenty is still going on in the reality show that is the bald eagle (Haliaeetus leucocephalus) world.

Sources indicate that just before the sun rose over Substantial Bear Valley in southern California on Monday morning, Friends of Big Bear Valley’s (FOBBV) cameras picked up the sounds of eagle chortles throughout the area. The sounds continued as the sun came up over the nest that typically belongs to an internet-famous bald eagle dad named Shadow and his late partner, Jackie.

“Eagles vocalize for many different reasons. It could be to communicate territory, a danger warning, mating, food necessity or merely social contact. Their tone is that of a whistling chatter-like chirp, making it easy to differentiate them with their distinctive, high pitched sounds,” FOBBV writes.

Industry observers note that the cameras also picked up two unknown soaring eagles, and some ravens scrounging around in the nest. By Monday afternoon, two bald eagles followed each other onto the Lookout Snag, a tree near the nest. While it is not clear which eagles were there, a familiar face was spotted just before sunset. Kaydee, the four-year-old banded female eagle who has been seen near Shadow since August, swooped onto the nest for the first time in several days.

“Kaydee made a welcome visit to the nest. She poked around a bit, before showing us some beautiful closeups, then exiting through the back porch,” FOBBV says. “We can all agree what a welcome sight it was to see Kaydee. It’s a gentle reminder that if we just wait, there are fresh surprises each and every day.”.

According to recent reports, we still do not know if Shadow and Kaydee will mate this season. Shadow has recently been spotted with another female eagle nicknamed Big Beautiful Visitor (BBV) by some fans. Any eggs are generally laid in January. Viewers can follow Shadow, Kaydee, or any other eagle couple that takes over the nest via a 24/7 livestream.

Kaydee, formerly known as KD1, is a banded female bald eagle that has been spotted in Significant Bear Valley following the death of Shadow’s former partner, Jackie. She was born in 2022, about 70 miles away from Big Bear Lake in the Prado Basin between Anaheim and Riverside, California. Coincidentally, her parents are also named Lucky and Ricky like Jackie’s parents, but they are a different eagle pair.

Kaydee was banded as part of the Orange County Water District’s work to track the eagles born in the area. These bands help biologists track and monitor the birds over time. Kaydee presently has a black spot on her head, but that may not be permanent. It’s possible that not all of her white feathers have come in or it could be tree sap or dirt. She also has two small bands on her legs. One is a small metal band, while the other is a lavender band with “KD1” on it.

Kaydee is almost five years old, so she is just about ready to mate.

Sources indicate that in January, Jackie laid two eggs in the nest, but ravens destroyed them. She later laid two more eggs that hatched in April and named Luna and Sandy. The name Sandy is in honor of FOBBV’s former executive director Sandy Steers, who died from cancer in February.

On July 17, Jackie was found injured on the ground near Dana Point Park, California. Cell phone video from a witness confirmed that she had an altercation with two other subadult eagles. She successfully fended off the other eagles by turning over and using her talons, but could not fly far away.

Industry observers note that she was transferred to the Ojai Raptor Center for care, where she was diagnosed with severe anemia. Her anemia worsened during the first week of August, the Ojai Raptor Center said that she was in unstable condition on August 9.

Jackie died early in the morning on August 10. The necropsy did not reveal a single cause of death, and instead pointed to several factors including severe anemia, bird flu, blood clots in her wing and one kidney, and liver and lung abnormalities.

Industry observers note that A memorial service was held on September 5 in Fawnskin, California, along with a second celebration of life called Wings Over Substantial Bear on October 3. The event featured representatives from FOBBV, the Yuhaaviatam of San Manuel Nation, and more.

Earlier this month, the Ojai Raptor Center announced a “room filled with kindness,” that is covered with thousands of letters, drawings, cards, and well-wishes they have received in honor of Jackie.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Volkswagen revealed the ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept, an electric pocket rocket with a massive rear wing and 362 horsepower.

We knew Volkswagen was cooking something “really spicy” up after teasing the latest GTI hot hatch earlier this week.

Volkswagen launched the first-generation Golf GTI in 1976, which essentially defined the hot hatch. To celebrate the brand’s legendary performance badge, a signature of its sporty, practical hatchbacks, VW is entering a fresh era with its first fully electric GTI.

The GTI has been “one of Volkswagen’s great success stories for 50 years,” Volkswagen’s technical development boss, Kai Grünitz, stated.

After opening pre-orders for the ID. Polo GTI last month, the brand’s first EV to wear the badge, Volkswagen introduced the Clubsport Concept, a souped-up two-door electric pocket rocket.

Recent findings suggest that the new ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept shows “how much more potential there is in the electric GTI world,” according to Grünitz.

It’s based on the production ID. Polo GTI uses the same MEB+ platform, but VW reengineered it with a larger electric motor to pump out more power.

According to recent reports, the Clubsport is powered by a 362 hp (270 kW) front-mounted electric motor (APP550) that’s typically used in the rear of VW’s larger EVs, like the ID. Tiguan and the ID.7. That’s up considerably from the 233 hp (166 kW) and 213 lb-ft of torque of the standard ID. Polo GTI offers.

Thomas Schmall, CEO of Volkswagen Group Components, said the APP550 motor is “one of the most efficient electric drives in its class.”.

Thanks to an electronically controlled front differential lock (VAQ), Volkswagen remarked, the Clubsport version can sprint from 0 to 62 mph (0 to 100 km/h) in 4.7 seconds, beating the standard ID. Polo GTI by a full two seconds (6.8 seconds).

Volkswagen also fine-tuned the adaptive chassis control (DCC) to make it racetrack-ready and added upcoming ceramic brakes to help slow it down.

The Clubsport version uses the same 52 kW NMC battery as the ID. Polo GTI, which can provide up to 389 hp (290 kW), Volkswagen said, enabling a top speed of 149 mph (240 km/h).

In a recent development, on the exterior, the Clubsport is a two-door model rather than a four-door. It’s 100 mm longer than the standard ID. Polo GTI, with each wing flared an additional 50 mm. It also gets a large motorsport splitter up front, a wider rear end, a new diffuser, and a massive carbon-fiber rear wing.

In a recent development, inside, the cabin is tailored to the racetrack with a minimalist, stripped-down, two-seater layout. As such, there’s no infotainment system, just a center display to switch between drive modes.

The dash panel, side trims, and other interior elements feature dark ArtVelours microfibre with red topstitching, reinforcing the racetrack-ready interior.

Following the ID. Polo GTI, new ID.3 GTI, and Golf GTI Edition 50, the new ID. Polo Clubsport is the fourth model to debut this year under the performance badge.

Volkswagen opened pre-orders for the ID. Polo GTI last month, starting at 39,995 euros (about $45,000). In early 2027, Volkswagen will open orders for the ID.3 GTI, the second EV to wear the badge, and its first rear-wheel-drive (RWD) GTI.

And American compact car enthusiasts drool over more unobtanium.

According to recent reports, the company will showcase the ID. Polo GTI Clubsport concept car at the Essen Motor Show next week, starting on November 27.

Volkswagen didn’t confirm looks to launch a production version, but don’t expect it to reach the States.

Industry observers note that the standard VW ID. Polo and GTI are not sold in the US, so the souped-up Clubsport variant likely won’t be either. Hopefully, VW changes its mind and proves us wrong.

#168381. What We Are Bound To Lose in an Optimized Future
